explanation: Tipping the horizon makes a scene feel uneasy. Carol Reed's The Third Man (1949) uses it again and again in the ruins of post-war Vienna.

claims.text: A Dutch angle is a shot in which the camera is tilted, so the horizon is not level.
A Dutch angle is not an overhead shot, a slow zoom or a shot through a window.
A tilted horizon is used to make a scene feel uneasy or disorienting.
Carol Reed's The Third Man (1949), set in post-war Vienna, makes heavy use of Dutch angles.
